analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek is a competent mid-tier IT services company with acceptable financials, but it sits outside my circle of competence, carries dangerously low promoter skin-in-the-game at 35.77%, and faces structural disruption from AI that I cannot properly price. At INR 1,746, the valuation is fair but not compelling enough to compensate for these quality concerns.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity at 0.20 is within acceptable range, and free cash flow is robust at INR 515 Cr in FY26 — OCF positive all 5 years
Valuation is modest — P/E of 12.8x and EV/EBITDA of 9.8x offers some margin of safety for a technology business
Revenue CAGR of 23.3% over 9 years with operating profit growing at 33% CAGR — the business has scaled profitably
key_risks: Promoter holding at 35.77% is well below my 55% floor — I will not invest where the founder is not fully committed
Finance costs exploded from INR 4 Cr (2017) to INR 44 Cr (2024) — a 10x rise signals growing leverage dependency even as revenues grew
IT services faces existential disruption from AI — I cannot predict which IT firms survive the next decade, and this uncertainty is unacceptable for a long-term hold
red_flags: Promoter holding at 35.77% — critically below my 55% minimum threshold; signals weak founder conviction
EBITDA dipped from INR 535 Cr (FY24) to INR 455 Cr (FY25) despite growing revenue — margin pressure is real
Borrowings nearly doubled from INR 273 Cr (FY21) to INR 583 Cr (FY25) — growth partly debt-funded
Not a consumer-facing business — I have no edge analyzing IT services demand cycles or client retention risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek has built a creditable business over four decades in enterprise IT, Oracle cloud, and digital services, with 23% revenue CAGR since 2017. The balance sheet is not broken — D/E at 0.20 passes my threshold, and free cash flow of INR 515 Cr in FY26 is healthy relative to its INR 5,412 Cr market cap. However, ROE at 15.6% is barely at my minimum, well short of the 18-22% I expect from core holdings, and the EBITDA dip in FY25 (535 → 455 Cr) reveals that margins are neither fortress-like nor consistent. Finance costs have ballooned 10x in a decade, which tells me growth has been partly bought, not organically earned.

The deal-breaker for me is the promoter holding of 35.77%. In my experience, the promoter's ownership level is the single loudest signal of conviction and alignment. When founders own less than 40% of their own business, I ask: why? Additionally, technology services is not my sector — I built DMart on predictable consumer demand, not on the shifting preferences of enterprise CIOs or government procurement cycles. AI is genuinely disrupting the IT services model, and I cannot assess with confidence whether Mastek's UK government and Oracle-heavy positioning provides durable protection or merely deferred obsolescence. I prefer to deploy capital where I sleep soundly.
